name: Lila Sciences, Inc.
subcategory: 'scientific superintelligence' + autonomous AI Science Factories (life science, chemistry, materials, energy)
origin_detail: Created in 2023 inside Flagship Pioneering, a venture-creation firm that remained its largest investor as of Mar 2025. Led by co-founder and CEO Geoffrey von Maltzahn, with co-founder and president Molly Gibson; John Gregoire is SVP of physical sciences.
flagship_projects: AI Science Factories (proprietary autonomous lab instruments)
MOSAIC multimodal flow matching for molecules and spectra (NeurIPS 2026)
openness_notes: Lila calls its AI Science Factory instruments 'proprietary'. Its news page links research papers (several arXiv preprints, Sep-Nov 2026, e.g. a Pd-oxide acidic-OER catalyst, 'The convergent laboratory', MOSAIC) and conference abstracts, but mentions no released models, datasets or code. Open preprints alone do not meet level 1 of the scale.

license_history.note: Papers posted to arXiv from 2026; no code, data or weights found

risk_events: Mar 2025: $200M seed (Flagship Pioneering, General Catalyst and others); revenue model 'still being determined'
15 Sep 2025: announced $235M Series A; 10 Oct 2025: closed a $350M Series A, total funding $550M
14 Oct 2025: Reuters headline 'AI lab Lila Sciences tops $1.3 billion valuation with new Nvidia backing'
22 Jul 2026: joined DOE's Genesis Mission with Phase I awards for three projects (Caltech, LBNL, Northwestern, Argonne, NLR)
No 2026 equity round appears on lila.ai/news as of Nov 2026
robustness: Well capitalized ($550M) with a deep-pocketed incubator (Flagship), NVIDIA backing and DOE project awards. But it is a single proprietary stack spanning very different domains (therapeutics, catalysts, materials), with no disclosed revenue. Nothing is open-sourced, so its assets would not survive outside the company.
physical_science_relevance: High. Target industries include advanced materials, energy, chemicals, oil and gas, and aerospace. Mar 2025 claims covered a non-iridium oxygen-evolution catalyst for green hydrogen and new carbon-capture sorbents. In Sep 2026 an AI-directed lab screened 2,942 green-hydrogen catalysts in three months, alongside a Pd-oxide acidic OER catalyst preprint. The DOE Genesis Mission projects are with national labs.
openness_effect_assessment: Closed by design: the pitch is proprietary 'AI Science Factory' hardware plus models trained on its own experimental data, with discoveries spun into products or companies (Flagship's playbook). Openness so far means preprints, which build scientific credibility and recruiting without releasing reusable assets. Its 2025 rounds suggest investors reward this closed-loop, proprietary-data model.
key_takeaway: Lila Sciences is the Flagship version of the 2025-2026 AI-for-science boom. It raised $550M in seven months of 2025, was valued above $1.3B with NVIDIA backing, and makes heavy physical-science claims (green-hydrogen catalysts, carbon-capture sorbents), all on proprietary instruments and data. It publishes papers but releases no models, data or code, so it shares results, not the means to reproduce them.
